provinces.name: Hrafnfjord
provinces.notes: Royal seat at the head of the great Hrafnfjord.

settlements.name: Kolvik
settlements.notes: Royal seat of Skarnheim at the head of the Hrafnfjord. The king's long hall stands above rows of boat-sheds where the realm's finest keels are laid, and master shipwrights here are honoured like minor jarls. A tidal race at the fjord narrows means no fleet arrives unannounced.

settlements.name: Skarfnes
settlements.notes: Fishing village on the outer skerries where the Hrafnfjord meets the Whale-Road. Its pilots guide strangers through the narrows for silver, and are suspected of steering the stingy onto the rocks.

settlements.name: Akrheim
settlements.notes: The only broad cornland in Hrafnfjord; it feeds the royal hall. Every Skarn jarl's son is sent here for a harvest to learn what bread costs, and the farm wives still tell which ones could swing a scythe.

settlements.name: Bjarkvik
settlements.notes: Birch-fringed inlet where the king's tar-boilers and charcoal-burners work for the Kolvik yards; the smoke can be seen from the fjord mouth.

settlements.name: Ytraheim
settlements.notes: A few fowlers' and seal-hunters' houses on the last isle before open ocean. They keep a beacon pile for the king and light it for anything with a sail; a long-nosed widow here hears all the gossip of the Whale-Road first.

settlements.name: Steinholt
settlements.notes: Jarl's seat in the stony upland dale, ringed by fields cleared one boulder at a time over generations. Its folk breed hardy horses and harder grudges: two kin-groups here have feuded over a single boundary stone for sixty years.

settlements.name: Grjotvik
settlements.notes: Steinvangr's harbour on a shingle bay of the southern shore, where the dale's horses, hides and quern-stones are loaded for the Straits.

settlements.name: Kvernadal
settlements.notes: Quarrymen cut quern-stones from the mountainside and sledge them down in winter; half the hand-mills in the North grind on Kvernadal stone.

settlements.name: Geitheim
settlements.notes: Goat-herders' high steading above the tree line. It shelters travellers caught by early snow, at a price the herders set after the snow has fallen.

settlements.name: Ulfshaug
settlements.notes: Jarl's seat on a ridge above the dark dale, named for the mound where the first jarl is said to have killed a wolf bare-handed. Wolf-skin cloaks mark the household men, and wolf bounties are paid in the hall every Yule.

settlements.name: Skuggvik
settlements.notes: Fjord village in a cleft so deep the sun does not touch its roofs from Yuledark to Icebreak. Its people are pale, patient and famously good at waiting out a siege.

settlements.name: Blotdal
settlements.notes: Temple-stead of the Skarn: a timber hof on the valley floor where the great Midwinter offerings are made. A hereditary priest family keeps its silver, its horses and its grudges; plundering it would turn every Skarn jarl against the plunderer.

settlements.name: Bratthaug
settlements.notes: Last steading below the mountain pass into Hvarnland. Its folk guide traders over the spine in summer and bury the unlucky ones in autumn.

settlements.name: Brimstad
settlements.notes: Jarl's seat on a surf-beaten headland whose hard approach has saved it from raiders more than once. Brimstad boatmen know every reef of the outer coast, including which ones the wreckers favour.

settlements.name: Sjodnes
settlements.notes: Salt-boilers' village: driftwood and peat fires burn day and night under iron pans of seawater, and the salt goes inland to every smokehouse in Skarnheim.

settlements.name: Gjallnes
settlements.notes: Fishing hamlet on a booming headland, so loud with surf in winter that its folk are said to shout even indoors.

settlements.name: Reynholt
settlements.notes: Farm hamlet among rowan woods in the hills behind Brimstad; its old wise-woman is consulted on cattle, marriages and weather, in that order.

settlements.name: Jarnvik
settlements.notes: Iron port of Skarnheim: bar-iron from the mountain mines and smelters is weighed on the jetty and shipped through the Straits. The ironmasters' feast decides more here than the jarl's Thing does.

settlements.name: Sindrastad
settlements.notes: Smelting village on Mjorvatn; slag heaps line the shore and the water runs rust-red after rain. Its smiths make the best axe-heads in the realm and say so.

settlements.name: Grafholt
settlements.notes: Charcoal-burners' hamlet in the dale woods below the mines; the pits smoke for weeks and the burners sleep beside them in turns.

settlements.name: Vardhaug
settlements.notes: Skarn border fort of turf and timber on a knoll above the pass into Hvarnland; its beacon can be seen from Jarnvik. The garrison changes every spring and complains every autumn.

settlements.name: Isholm
settlements.notes: Northernmost jarl's seat of Skarnheim on a rocky holm in the Rimesea, shut in by ice until Icebreak is out. Walrus ivory, eiderdown and dried cod go south with the first ships, and the first crew in each spring is feasted for a week.

settlements.name: Hrimvik
settlements.notes: Walrus- and seal-hunters' village; its boats push farther into the Rimesea than anyone else's, and fewer come back than leave.

settlements.name: Fjallheim
settlements.notes: Herders' hamlet in the one green valley of Kaldbrekka, under snowfields that feed its meadows all summer.

settlements.name: Tindnes
settlements.notes: Eider-down gatherers on a ness below sharp peaks; they climb the bird cliffs on ropes of twisted hide.

settlements.name: Hvarnsted
settlements.notes: Royal seat of Hvarnland on the shore of Malvatn, reached from the sea by karvi up the Strom. Three great grave-mounds of the old kings overlook the hall, and the king sits on the middle one to hear suits at the spring Thing.

settlements.name: Vesholm
settlements.notes: Temple-stead on a holm in Langsjo, joined to the shore by a timber causeway. Offerings to Valgrim and Fjorna are made in its grove; the temple's priests are the king's kin and his best informants.

settlements.name: Tingshavn
settlements.notes: Ferry harbour facing Thingey. At midsummer its strand fills with the booths and boats of everyone bound for the Allthing, and its ale-wives make a year's silver in two weeks.

settlements.name: Rorholm
settlements.notes: Reed-cutters' hamlet on the western shore; Rorholm thatch roofs half the halls of Aldmark.

settlements.name: Galtsted
settlements.notes: Swineherds' hamlet where the oak woods of southern Aldmark run down into the fens; its boar-hunts are the royal household's favourite autumn sport.

settlements.name: Elgholm
settlements.notes: Jarl's seat among the wide forests, on a holm at the marsh edge where elk come down to drink. Fur-traders from all over the North meet at its winter fair, when the bogs freeze hard enough for sledges.

settlements.name: Skinnhavn
settlements.notes: Fur harbour on the Rimesea shore, where marten, beaver and bear pelts are baled for the summer ships and graded by an old trapper who has never once been fooled.

settlements.name: Mardsted
settlements.notes: Trappers' hamlet deep in the forest; its people pay their skat in marten skins and speak to strangers as little as possible.

settlements.name: Orreskog
settlements.notes: Forest hamlet of grouse-snarers and honey-hunters; its mead is better than the jarl's, which the jarl knows.

settlements.name: Vassby
settlements.notes: Jarl's seat in the lake country, where there is more water than land; its folk go everywhere by boat in summer and over the ice in winter. Famous for eel-traps, and for a jarl who settles small disputes by fishing contest.

settlements.name: Lomholm
settlements.notes: Lake village of reed-thatched houses on Elgsjo; loons call all night in summer and the boat-builders here make the lightest skiffs in Hvarnland.

settlements.name: Laxhavn
settlements.notes: Salmon weirs at the mouth of the Vassa; the hamlet owes the Vassby jarl one fish in ten, and argues every year about which ten.

settlements.name: Ingsted
settlements.notes: Upland farm hamlet under the mountain spine, where Skarn and Hvarn herders share the summer pastures and quarrel over them.

settlements.name: Myrhavn
settlements.notes: Jarl's seat and harbour where the iron bogs drain into the Gray Firth. Bog-iron blooms come down the Elgsa on rafts; the jarl takes every tenth bloom and is rich for it.

settlements.name: Slaggsted
settlements.notes: Bog-iron village in the Gyllenmyr: ore is raked from the bog bottoms, roasted and smelted in clay furnaces. The smoke is everywhere, and so is the cough.

settlements.name: Torvholm
settlements.notes: Peat-cutters' hamlet on a dry rise beside the Ljoma; Torvholm turves feed the furnaces of Slaggsted.

settlements.name: Sikhavn
settlements.notes: Whitefish netters on the Gray Firth shore, who smoke their catch over alder and trade it for iron.

settlements.name: Bjornstad
settlements.notes: Jarl's seat in the bear-forests near the eastern marches. Its doorposts are carved with bears, and the jarl's champions wear bearskins to the Thing, which the lawspeakers wish they would not.

settlements.name: Hidholm
settlements.notes: Lake village on Bjornvatn, where bear-hunters winter. Its hall holds a bear skull for every jarl of Bjornskog, and a wolf skull for a jarl nobody mentions.

settlements.name: Kalvhavn
settlements.notes: Harbour at the Kalva mouth on the Gray Firth, where timber is rafted down for the shipyards of the south.

settlements.name: Tjarsted
settlements.notes: Tar-burners' hamlet near the eastern marches. Velkar traders come over the border for its pine tar, not always peacefully.

settlements.name: Austhavn
settlements.notes: Jarl's seat and the gateway east: ships bound for the Velkar rivers fit out here, and Velkar furs, wax and eastern silver come back. Velkar merchants keep a winter house in the town and a priest of the River Spirits with it.

settlements.name: Leidhavn
settlements.notes: River-mouth harbour at the Strom; every karvi bound up to Hvarnsted pays the king's river-toll here, and the toll-reeve is the richest man in Austrvik after the jarl.

settlements.name: Skarvholm
settlements.notes: Fishing hamlet on the long isle in the Gray Firth, white with cormorant droppings; its men pilot ships through the firth skerries.

settlements.name: Hjortsted
settlements.notes: Hunting hamlet on the road to Hvarnsted; the king's deer-park keepers live here and hang poachers by the road.

settlements.name: Sundby
settlements.notes: Royal seat of Eyjamark, its hall on a low green rise above the Straits. Every passing ship dips its sail to Sundby and pays toll at the king's jetty; those that do not are remembered.

settlements.name: Ravstrand
settlements.notes: Amber-gatherers comb this south strand after every autumn storm; the best pieces go to Kaupholm and the rest into the hair of every bride in Eyjamark.

settlements.name: Tangby
settlements.notes: Kelp-burners and fishers on the western shore; the hamlet smells of seaweed ash from spring to autumn.

settlements.name: Gormsvik
settlements.notes: Herring hamlet on the eastern shore; in a good season the shoals run so thick the boats are rowed back half-sunk.

settlements.name: Lyngvik
settlements.notes: Jarl's seat on a heather island in the narrows of the Straits. Its jarls collect a second toll a day's sail before Sundby's and call it a courtesy.

settlements.name: Hedstrand
settlements.notes: Sheep hamlet on the island's southern heath; its wool is coarse, its weavers are not.

settlements.name: Ternvik
settlements.notes: Egg-gatherers' hamlet on the western shore, where the terns nest in thousands and attack anyone who comes near.

settlements.name: Hornby
settlements.notes: Jarl's seat on the northern horn of the Eyjar mainland, facing the Whale-Road and the Straits at once. Its jarls grow rich on pilotage and quarrel with Sundby over who may charge for it.

settlements.name: Kobbevik
settlements.notes: Seal-hunting village on the Whale-Road shore; seal oil lights the halls of half Eyjamark.

settlements.name: Dynby
settlements.notes: Hamlet among the dunes facing Lyngey, half buried by drifting sand every few winters and dug out again.

settlements.name: Mosstead
settlements.notes: Jarl's seat on the bog island of Mosey: low turf halls, cattle and peat. Its jarls are known for long memories and short speeches.

settlements.name: Hargstrand
settlements.notes: Temple-stead of the Eyjar: a stone harg above a bog pool where offerings have been sunk for longer than anyone can count. Weapons, rings and once a whole boat lie in the peat, and the priestess knows where each one went down.

settlements.name: Ebbvik
settlements.notes: Mud-flat hamlet at the western tip; at low water its folk walk out a mile to gather cockles.

settlements.name: Sandvik
settlements.notes: Jarl's seat on a long sand bay of the Whale-Road coast; ships are hauled up on rollers rather than moored. Its jarl breeds the horses of the Strand-Riders.

settlements.name: Vadstrand
settlements.notes: Village at the head of the inner fjord where the coast road fords the stream; cattle drovers and their herds pass through every autumn.

settlements.name: Hjortvik
settlements.notes: Trading village on the eastern shore facing Mosey; Corvani wine merchants winter here rather than face the open Whale-Road.

settlements.name: Kjarrby
settlements.notes: Heath hamlet among scrub and bog; its folk cut peat, keep bees and distrust everyone from beyond the next ridge.

settlements.name: Skjoldby
settlements.notes: Border fortress where a turf rampart and ditch cross the neck of the land against Saxmark. Sundby pays the garrison in silver; the local farmers pay it in complaints.

settlements.name: Kaupholm
settlements.notes: The great market of the North on a low island in the Straits. Each summer its booth-streets fill with Skarn iron, Hvarn furs, Albric wool, Corvani wine and eastern silver. The market peace is sworn on the harbour stone; breaking it means outlawry in every realm.

settlements.name: Kramby
settlements.notes: Pedlars' hamlet on the south shore, where small traders too poor for a Kaupholm booth sell from their boats.

settlements.name: Skelstrand
settlements.notes: Shell-strand hamlet whose folk burn shells for lime and mend the market booths for a living.

settlements.name: Hallowed Plain
settlements.notes: Neutral holy ground of the whole North. The Allthing meets here every Highsun 15, and the empty High Seat stands on its stone platform at the head of the plain. A lawspeaker's household keeps it the year round; bloodshed here means outlawry everywhere.

sites.name: Saltha's Throat
sites.notes: Sea-cave on the outer Saltnes coast that booms at storm-tide; coast-folk say a sunken temple bell rings inside. Wreckers den in its upper galleries, and the lower passages flood with every tide.

sites.name: Tower of the Hooded
sites.notes: A lonely stone-footed watchtower on a hill between the lakes, kept by an old fellowship of rune-masters who call themselves the Raven-Speakers. They answer questions with riddles and remember everyone who climbs the hill.

sites.name: Oath-Mound
sites.notes: The old Thing-mound of the Eyjar, older than Sundby. A hereditary warden keeps the stone on its crown and meets any challenger in holmgang; no one has sworn falsely on it in living memory, or so the warden says.

sites.name: Ashbarrow
sites.notes: A burnt grave-mound in the bear-forest, raised over a hall fired with its dead inside. An outcast band of Skell's fire-priests still tends it; they pack its passages with pitch and kindling, and teach fire-craft to anyone they judge worthy.

sites.name: Hidden-Fjord Wreck
sites.notes: A great ship lies on its side at the head of a fjord that cannot be seen from the sea, its hull wedged between rock and ice. The tide uncovers the hold for an hour at the lowest ebbs.

sites.name: First Wolf Hollow
sites.notes: A ring of old stones in a forest hollow where, the hunters say, the first wolf-coat warriors were made. A great wolf pack dens in the rocks above and has never been driven out.

sites.name: High Barrow
sites.notes: Grave-mound of the first High King at the head of the Hallowed Plain, sealed with stone. A hereditary barrow-warden opens it only to the holder of a kingdom crown or the bearer of the Raven-Speakers' quill, and fights anyone else who tries.

sites.name: Raven Cleft
sites.notes: A cleft cave in the mountain wall above the dark dale; ravens nest at its mouth and outlaws have used its dry inner chamber.

sites.name: the Ice-Kettle
sites.notes: A meltwater cave under the snowfields; it floods without warning in summer and freezes shut in winter.

sites.name: Outlaws' Hole
sites.notes: A cave high in the Steinvangr crags where outlawed men have hidden for generations; the current band is led by a former hirdman of Steinholt.

sites.name: Gray Bear Cave
sites.notes: A rock cave in the eastern forest where a huge old bear winters; the Bjornstad hunters dare each other to go in and mostly do not.

sites.name: the Ship-Howe
sites.notes: A long mound on the hill above the fjord, raised over a sea-king and his ship; Kolvik shipwrights pour ale on it before a keel is laid.

sites.name: Seven Howes
sites.notes: Seven grave-mounds in a row across the heath. Nobody agrees whose they are, and one has been dug into recently.

sites.name: Drowned Men's Howe
sites.notes: A mound raised for sailors lost at sea, with stones set for every ship; the widows of Saltnes still bring offerings.

sites.name: Heath Howe
sites.notes: A heather-grown mound in the middle of Lyngey with a collapsed passage on its seaward side.

sites.name: the Widow's Hall
sites.notes: A jarl's hall burned with its household inside during an old feud; only the jarl's widow came out, and she still owns the land. Squatters live in the outbuildings, and her grandsons want the burners' kin found.

sites.name: Coldhearth
sites.notes: A steading abandoned after a famine winter; its roof timbers are still sound, and someone has lit fires in it lately.

sites.name: the Broken Knarr
sites.notes: A merchant ship broken on the reef off the Whale-Road shore; the Kobbevik folk have salvaged most of it, but not the strongbox.

sites.name: the Toll-Dodger
sites.notes: A ship that tried to slip through the Straits by night without paying toll, and found a reef instead. Its cargo was never recovered.

sites.name: the Narrows Beacon
sites.notes: An old timber beacon-tower at the northern tip of Lyngey, overlooking the narrows; abandoned since the toll-keepers moved to Lyngvik, but not empty.

sites.name: the Hanging Grove
sites.notes: A grove of ancient ash trees where offerings were once hung in the branches; the custom has lapsed, but the bones of the last ones still hang there.

sites.name: Rowan Grove
sites.notes: Sacred rowan grove in the Steinvangr dale where the folk make offerings for the harvest and swear betrothals.
